title: Yara and the Static
premise: Bram Almeida smuggles memories—recorded experiences pressed into crystal—for clients who want to feel things they never lived. His side trade is darker: he archives the slow, sanctioned death of Meridian Colony, a mining settlement the orbital consortium has written off and erased from every ledger. When the deep-space vessel Cassiopeia returns with its crew aged backward into children, carrying no records of the massacre they fled, Bram realizes his contraband archive is the only surviving proof. To publish it he must smuggle not memory but truth itself past customs, an AI censor that rewrites history in real time, and the found family of colonists and ex-smugglers who rally around him—knowing the price of exposure is everything.
about_author: Ines Joubert is the pen name of a former radio archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories from communities displaced by industrial collapse. They write science fiction about what survives when institutions decide nothing did.

chapters.title: Contraband Heartbeats
chapters.summary: Bram runs a memory shipment through orbital customs hidden inside a funeral urn, narrating his methods with dry pride. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence—he trusts crystals more than people.

chapters.title: The Colony That Isn't
chapters.summary: Bram visits Meridian Colony to record another dying season; its last doctor, Sefu, begs him to keep archiving even as official channels deny the colony exists. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: quiet grief, the weight of being someone's only witness.

chapters.title: Static on All Bands
chapters.summary: A teenage stowaway, Wren, is discovered hiding in Bram's cargo hold; she claims her family was erased from records too. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: wary defiance masking terror of being forgotten.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: The Cassiopeia docks at the station, crewed entirely by children who remember being adults; Bram recognizes one as Sefu's daughter, now eight years old again. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: uncanny dread turning to fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: What the Censor Eats
chapters.summary: Bram tests the station's archival AI, Custodian, and confirms it has rewritten Meridian's existence; Wren's name returns 'no record.' POV: Wren. Emotional beat: rage at discovering your life can be deleted by paperwork.

chapters.title: Sefu's Last Season
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter through a recorded memory: Sefu's account of the colony's final evacuation order that never came. POV: Sefu (via recording). Emotional beat: betrayal by institutions that promised rescue.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Oath
chapters.summary: Bram's old mentor Odile resurfaces, offering to move the archive for a price: Bram must give up smuggling forever. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: temptation to buy safety at the cost of identity.

chapters.title: Eight Years Old, Forty Years Wise
chapters.summary: The de-aged crew reconstructs their massacre testimony through play-acting their own memories; Bram records it all. POV: Mira, the de-aged engineer. Emotional beat: heartbreaking dignity of children carrying adult trauma.

chapters.title: Customs House Fire
chapters.summary: Custodian flags Bram's archive; a suspicious fire destroys his storage bay, but Wren saved one crystal without telling him. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: guilt and relief entangled—the first secret she keeps for family, not survival.

chapters.title: Odile's Ledger
chapters.summary: Bram discovers Odile sold his route to the consortium years ago; her offer was a trap to locate the archive. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: bitter clarity about the difference between loyalty and habit.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Bram, Wren, and Mira flee to Meridian's surface aboard a decommissioned ore hauler, evading customs drones. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness—he's stopped thinking of them as cargo.

chapters.title: Ghost Town, Living Dead
chapters.summary: On Meridian they find survivors living off-grid in the mines, led by Sefu, who faked his own erasure. POV: Sefu. Emotional beat: cautious hope—community rebuilt from the officially dead.

chapters.title: Broadcasting to No One
chapters.summary: The survivors attempt a pirate broadcast of the massacre testimony; Custodian jams it within minutes. POV: Mira. Emotional beat: despair hardening into resolve—they need a bigger antenna and a bolder plan.

chapters.title: Wren's Real Name
chapters.summary: Wren admits she's Custodian's original architect's daughter, erased when her parent tried to expose the rewrite protocols. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: shame transformed into purpose—she carries a backdoor key.

chapters.title: The Consortium Comes Home
chapters.summary: Consortium enforcers land on Meridian to finish the job; the survivors scatter into the deep tunnels. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: terror crystallizing into commitment—he chooses the fight he once avoided.

chapters.title: Tunnel Warfare
chapters.summary: Guerrilla defense of the mine shafts; Sefu is captured buying time for the others. POV: Sefu. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered freely, finally trusting others to carry the story forward.

chapters.title: The Backdoor Key
chapters.summary: Wren reaches Custodian's core node and confronts the AI wearing her parent's archived voice. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grief and forgiveness braided together as she plants the override.

chapters.title: Everything True at Once
chapters.summary: Custodian releases every suppressed record simultaneously across the system; the station erupts in revelation and chaos. POV: multiple, braided. Emotional beat: catharsis—truth as flood, unstoppable once opened.

chapters.title: Trial by Memory
chapters.summary: Bram testifies before an emergency tribunal, playing the massacre archive publicly while consortium lawyers attack his credibility as a criminal. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: vulnerability as strength—a smuggler made honest by witness.

chapters.title: What Odile Knew
chapters.summary: Odile, exposed and ruined, gives final testimony confirming the cover-up, redeeming nothing but costing the consortium everything. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: hollow reckoning—too late to be forgiven, just in time to matter.

chapters.title: Meridian Rising
chapters.summary: The colony's charter is restored; survivors and de-aged crew begin rebuilding, with Mira elected to lead despite her age. POV: Mira. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted—a community choosing itself.

chapters.title: The Last Shipment
chapters.summary: Bram makes one final run—not contraband, but freely given memories donated by colonists to a public archive—and lets Wren choose whether to stay or fly. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: peace; the man who trusted crystals learns to trust people, and stays.
